**Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding** — new joiners hit the floor with zero standardisation; no intake form capture, fitness assessment protocol, or first-class experience template. Direct revenue leak.
- **Cancellation & Churn** — no documented win-back trigger, exit interview process, or pause-vs-cancel decision tree. You're losing members silently.
- **Class Quality Audit Checklist** — coaches operate in a vacuum; no baseline standard for cueing, energy, music, timing, or member modification acknowledgment.
- **Member Checkins** — retention magic happens in month 2–3; no scheduled touchpoint SOP, NPS capture, or struggle-detection cadence.
- **Coaching Development Roadmap** — 20/23 coach SOPs exist but nothing maps progression, certification, or performance calibration over time.
- **Member data privacy & GDPR** — high-risk gap for a gym holding photos, payment, health data, and email lists in the UK.
- **Complaints & Incidents** — no escalation protocol, documentation standard, or resolution SLA (injury, billing, harassment, facility issues).
- **30 Day Goals & Member Outcomes** — no framework to set baseline goals at signup or measure progress; undermines retention psychology and testimonial capture.

**Needs updating**

- **Referral Programme SOP** — likely exists but missing: referrer reward mechanics, referee discount timing, tracking/attribution, and comms cadence to active members.
- **Member Pause SOP** — if it exists, gaps are almost certain around: pause length limits, re-engagement comms during pause, and conversion-back rates.
- **Milestone Achievements SOP** — missing celebration framework (who triggers it, comms template, social proof capture, member recognition).
- **Weekly Key Coach Tasks** — exists?

# THE FORGE — FRACTIONAL CFO ACTION PLAN

## 🚨 HEADLINE: JULY IS A CRISIS MONTH
Revenue collapsed to £1,363 (93% down from June £17,711). Active clients held at 151, but revenue per member dropped to £9.03/month vs £120.48 in June. This is NOT a trading issue — **this is a data/billing problem**. Investigate immediately: payment processing failure, invoicing not sent, system error, or members on trial/pause. Fix this before any other action.

---

## INCREASE REVENUE

• **Fix July billing catastrophe first** — £1,363 revenue on 151 active clients should be ~£18–19k. Audit payment gateway, resend invoices, check member status records. This is your single biggest priority.

• **Raise base membership price** — June and May averaged £165–171 AR/M; September–December baseline was £145–162. You're leaving £5–15/month per member on the table vs Q4 pricing. Test a 10–15% price increase (£12–18/month uplift) on new sign-ups immediately; grandfather existing members for 3 months, then migrate.

• **Cap and monetise the churn spike** — January–April ran 5.7–8.3% monthly churn; June/July dropped to 0%. Reverse that momentum: audit leavers from Jan–April (what happened?), implement exit-survey upsell (12-month commitment discount, personal training bundle), re-engagement campaign for those 40+ members you lost Q1.

• **Upsell personal training and class packs** — You have 151 active members in a studio "roughly twice the size" but no PT revenue line visible. Launch tiered PT offer (£25/session intro, £200/10-pack). Target 15–20% uptake = £500–700/month new recurring revenue within 60 days.

• **Fill quiet class slots with off-peak pricing** — No capacity data given, but assume lower-demand time slots exist. Offer "off-peak pass" (£15/month, 6am or 2pm classes only) to retain price-sensitive members and smooth utilisation.

# Service Menu Build: Concrete Execution for The Forge

• **Start with your top 5 revenue streams TODAY.** Don't design a menu from scratch—list what you're actually selling right now (group classes, PT, memberships, challenges, etc.). For each, write: exact price, exactly what's included, and what's NOT included. This takes 2 hours, not 2 weeks.

• **Make TWO separate docs, not one confusing hybrid.** Coach version = what they sell + commission/incentive structure + how to position each tier. Member version = clean pricing tiers with clear outcome language ("Lose 8lbs in 12 weeks" beats "12-week program"). Coaches need permission to upsell; members need clarity to buy.

• **Price defensively with anchoring.** Your premium PT tier should feel expensive next to group classes—use it to make mid-tier packages look like the "smart choice." If your highest PT rate is £45/session, your mid-tier (4-session bundles) suddenly feels better value at £40/session. Test this with your top 3 coaches first.

• **Build in a decision trigger for coaches.** Add one line: "If member says X, recommend Y package." This removes guesswork. Example: "Member unsure about commitment → suggest 6-week challenge package first, then PT add-on." Coaches close more when they have a script.

• **Publish internally this week, test for 2 weeks, then iterate.** Share with your coaches Friday, gather their friction points by Wednesday, adjust by Friday. Your members are your real focus—get coaches comfortable selling first.

**Insights**

1. **July was an anomaly, not a plateau.** You nailed something in July—215 leads at £2/lead with 29 sales (13% close rate)—then August collapsed to 82 leads despite similar spend. That's not market fatigue; it's creative or targeting decay. You've likely exhausted a winning audience or the ad creative stopped performing after saturation.

2. **August's higher close rate (29% vs July's 13%) proves your sales process works.** The problem isn't conversion; it's lead volume and quality. Fewer leads in August means fewer sales, even though each lead is more "qualified" (closer rate). You're not scaling—you're shrinking.

3. **Cost-per-lead has doubled since July (£2 to £5), but you're still profitable.** At £52 profit per trial, you're healthy. But July showed you could do this at half the CPA. That gap is your immediate opportunity: find what made July work and resurrect it.

If July repeats, you've found your repeatable engine.
